title: CmdPal: Redesign the Performance Monitor Memory card

proposed_comments.title: Distinguish the headline from the composition label

confidence.rationale: The pinned template binds the headline to UsedMem; the composition uses MemInUse, and UsedMemory is an existing localized label for the former.

proposed_comments.body:
### Distinguish the headline from the composition label

**Severity:** `medium`

The headline displays `UsedMem`, which includes modified pages, while the composition’s “In use” segment displays `MemInUse`, which excludes them. When modified pages are present, users see two different amounts under the same label; use the existing “In use (compressed)” resource for the headline.

```suggestion
                  "text": "%Memory_Widget_Template/UsedMemory%"
```

proposed_comments.title: Localize the memory-speed format

confidence.rationale: The exact producer embeds the format while nearby widget values use resource-based formatting; the numeric speed remains correctly supplied.

proposed_comments.body:
### Localize the memory-speed format

**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.PerformanceMonitor/PerformanceWidgetsPage.cs` (the `memSpeed` producer) and `src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.PerformanceMonitor/Strings/en-US/Resources.resw` (the Memory widget resources).

**Problem:** The producer embeds the English `{0} MT/s` format in code. The number already uses current-culture formatting, but translators cannot change the unit’s placement or spacing through a resource.

**Why it matters:** The numeric speed remains correct and the `MT/s` unit is present; this is a low-severity presentation/localization limitation, not data loss or a functional reading error. Some locales may prefer different spacing or ordering.

**Suggested change:**
1. Add a `Memory_Widget_Template.Speed_Value` format resource with `{0} MT/s` and a translator comment explaining the placeholder and unit.
2. In `PerformanceWidgetsPage.cs`, format `modules.SpeedMegaTransfers` using `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture` and `Resources.GetResource("Memory_Widget_Template/Speed_Value")` instead of embedding the literal.

**Verification:** Build the Performance Monitor unit-test project with the new producer/resource pairing. Verify the English value still renders as, for example, `5600 MT/s`, and validate localized resource entries retain one numeric placeholder while permitting locale-appropriate spacing/order. The paired implementation was compiled in the pinned literal candidate; no separate localized runtime rendering test is claimed.

proposed_comments.title: Saturate the in-use remainder when samples disagree

confidence.rationale: The separately sampled UsedMem and MemModified values feed separate composition segments, and the pinned fallback can count UsedMem twice when the modified counter is at least as large.

proposed_comments.body:
### Saturate the in-use remainder when samples disagree

**Severity:** `medium`

`UsedMem` and `MemModified` come from separate samples, so a transient skew can make `MemModified` equal or exceed `UsedMem`. In that case the fallback counts all of `UsedMem` as in-use while the composition also adds `MemModified`, so the displayed composition can double-count bytes and overstate its total. Clamp the remainder to zero in that branch.

```suggestion
    public ulong MemInUse => UsedMem > MemModified ? UsedMem - MemModified : 0;
```
